title: Alice in Wonderland
author: Lewis Carroll
ru: Девочка Алиса падает в кроличью нору и попадает в странную страну, где всё наоборот.

chapters.title: Chapter 1. Down the Rabbit Hole
chapters.text:
Alice is a young girl. She is sitting by a river with her sister. It is a hot summer day. Her sister is reading a book. The book has no pictures and no talks in it. Alice is bored.

Suddenly, a white rabbit runs past her. The rabbit has pink eyes. He is wearing a jacket, and he has a watch.

“Oh dear! Oh dear! I am late!” says the Rabbit. He looks at his watch and runs away.

Alice is very surprised. A rabbit with a watch? She jumps up and runs after him. The Rabbit goes into a big hole under a tree. Alice goes into the hole too.

The hole is very deep. Alice is falling and falling. She is falling slowly. She can see cupboards and shelves on the walls. She can see maps and pictures. She takes a jar from a shelf. The jar says “ORANGE MARMALADE”, but it is empty.

“How long am I falling?” she thinks. “Am I near the centre of the Earth?”

Then, bump! Alice is on the ground. She is not hurt. She stands up and looks around. The White Rabbit is running down a long hall.

“Oh, my ears and whiskers! It is so late!” he says. Then he is gone.

chapters.title: Chapter 2. The Pool of Tears
chapters.text:
Alice is in a long hall. There are many doors, but they are all locked. On a glass table, she finds a very small gold key. Behind a curtain, there is a little door. The key opens it! Behind the door, Alice can see a beautiful garden with flowers and fountains. But the door is very small. Alice is too big.

On the table, there is now a little bottle. It says “DRINK ME”. Alice drinks it. It tastes of cherry, cake and toffee. Now she is very small, only twenty-five centimetres tall! But the key is on the table, and she can't reach it.

Then Alice sees a little cake. It says “EAT ME”. She eats it. Now she is growing and growing. Her head is touching the ceiling! She is three metres tall.

“Curiouser and curiouser!” says Alice.

She is very sad, and she starts to cry. Her tears are big. Soon there is a pool of tears in the hall.

The White Rabbit comes back. He has white gloves and a fan. Alice speaks to him, but he is afraid. He drops the gloves and the fan and runs away. Alice takes the fan. Now she is getting small again! She is swimming in her own tears. A mouse is swimming there too.

chapters.title: Chapter 3. Advice from a Caterpillar
chapters.text:
Alice is in a big wood now. She is very small. The flowers and the grass are taller than her. Near her, there is a big mushroom. Alice stands on her toes and looks over the top.

A big blue caterpillar is sitting on the mushroom. He is smoking a long pipe. He is quiet. He looks at Alice for a long time.

“Who are you?” asks the Caterpillar.

“I don't know, sir,” says Alice. “I know who I am in the morning. But I am changing all day. I am big, then I am small. It is very confusing.”

“It is not confusing,” says the Caterpillar.

“Maybe it is not confusing for you,” says Alice. “But one day you are going to be a butterfly. That is strange too, don't you think?”

“Not at all,” says the Caterpillar.

Alice wants to leave. “Come back!” says the Caterpillar. “Keep your temper.”

“Is that all?” asks Alice.

“No,” he says. After a long time, he gets down from the mushroom. “One side makes you taller. The other side makes you shorter.”

“One side of what?” asks Alice.

“Of the mushroom,” he says, and he goes away into the grass.

Alice takes a little piece from each side. Now she can be big or small. She can choose!

chapters.title: Chapter 4. The Cheshire Cat
chapters.text:
Alice is walking in the wood. She sees a small house. She goes inside. It is the house of the Duchess. The kitchen is full of smoke and pepper. The Cook is making soup with a lot of pepper. The Duchess is sitting on a chair with a baby. The baby is crying and crying. Everyone is sneezing.

Only one animal is not sneezing. It is a big cat, and it is sitting by the fire. It is smiling from ear to ear.

“Why is your cat smiling?” asks Alice.

“It is a Cheshire cat,” says the Duchess. “That's why.”

Later, Alice is in the wood again. The Cheshire Cat is sitting in a tree. It is still smiling.

“Please, which way can I go from here?” asks Alice.

“That depends on where you want to go,” says the Cat.

“Then it doesn't matter which way you go,” says the Cat. “In that direction lives a Hatter. In that direction lives a March Hare. Visit them. They are both mad.”

“But I don't want to be with mad people,” says Alice.

“Oh, you can't help that,” says the Cat. “We are all mad here. I am mad. You are mad.”

Then the Cat slowly disappears. First its tail, then its body. At the end, only its smile is there.

chapters.title: Chapter 5. A Mad Tea Party
chapters.text:
There is a table under a tree in front of a house. The March Hare and the Hatter are having tea. A small animal, the Dormouse, is sitting between them. He is sleeping.

“No room! No room!” they say.

“There is a lot of room!” says Alice, and she sits in a big chair.

“Have some wine,” says the March Hare.

Alice looks at the table. “I can't see any wine,” she says.

“There isn't any,” says the March Hare.

The Hatter looks at Alice. “Why is a raven like a writing desk?” he asks.

Alice likes riddles. She thinks and thinks. “I don't know. What is the answer?”

“I don't know,” says the Hatter.

“Nor do I,” says the March Hare.

The Hatter has a watch. It shows the day, not the hour. “It is always six o'clock here,” he says. “It is always tea time. So we have no time to wash the cups. We move around the table to clean cups.”

Then the Dormouse wakes up and starts a story. It is a very strange story about three sisters in a well.

The Hatter and the March Hare are putting the Dormouse into the teapot. Alice is angry. “This is the silliest tea party in my life!” she says, and she walks away.

chapters.title: Chapter 6. The Queen of Hearts
chapters.text:
At last, Alice finds the beautiful garden. There is a big rose tree. The roses are white, but three gardeners are painting them red. The gardeners look like playing cards.

“Why are you painting the roses?” asks Alice.

“This must be a red rose tree,” says one gardener. “We are planting a white one by mistake. The Queen is going to be very angry!”

Then the Queen of Hearts comes, with the King and many cards. The White Rabbit is there too. The Queen sees the roses.

“Off with their heads!” she shouts.

The Queen is always angry. She says “Off with their heads!” all the time.

“Can you play croquet?” she asks Alice.

“Yes!” says Alice.

It is a very strange game. The balls are hedgehogs. The mallets are flamingos. The cards are the arches. The flamingo doesn't want to play. It is looking at Alice all the time. The hedgehogs are walking away. Everyone is playing at the same time and shouting.

The Cheshire Cat's head appears in the air. “How are you getting on?” it asks.

“It is not fair,” says Alice. “There are no rules.”

The King doesn't like the Cat. “Off with its head!” says the Queen. But the Cat has only a head and no body. How can they cut it off? Nobody knows!

chapters.title: Chapter 7. Who Stole the Tarts?
chapters.text:
There is a trial in a big room. The King and the Queen of Hearts are sitting on their thrones. The Knave of Hearts is standing in front of them. On a table, there is a plate of tarts.

The White Rabbit reads: “The Queen of Hearts makes some tarts. The Knave of Hearts steals them!”

The first witness is the Hatter. He is very nervous.

Now Alice is feeling strange. She is growing again! She is getting bigger and bigger.

“Call the next witness!” says the King. “Alice!”

Alice stands up. She is very big now, and she knocks over the jury box.

“What do you know about this?” asks the King.

“Nothing,” says Alice.

“Rule forty-two,” says the King. “All persons more than a mile high must leave the court.”

“I am not a mile high!” says Alice.

“Off with her head!” shouts the Queen. Nobody moves.

“Who cares for you?” says Alice. “You are only a pack of cards!”

The cards fly up into the air and fall on her. Alice screams. Then she opens her eyes. She is lying by the river.

“Wake up, Alice! You are sleeping a long time!”

“Oh, I am having a very strange dream!” says Alice, and she tells her sister all about Wonderland.
